lessons.title: Time and Work Basics
lessons.concept: If A can complete work in n days, A's 1 day's work = 1/n. Work = Rate × Time. Total work often treated as 1 unit.
lessons.formula: 1 day's work = 1/n; Work done = rate × days
lessons.worked_example: A completes work in 50 days → 1 day's work = 1/50. 70 men in 5 days: total = 20×50=1000 man-days; done = 70×5=350; % = 350/1000 = 35%.

lessons.title: Combined Work
lessons.concept: If A and B together complete in a days and B alone in b days, A alone = ab/(b−a) days. Combined rate = sum of individual rates.
lessons.worked_example: A+B in 15 days, B alone in 20. A alone = (15×20)/(20−15) = 300/5 = 60 days.

lessons.title: Work and Wages
lessons.concept: Wages are distributed in proportion to work done (1/day rate). If A:B rates are rA:rB, wages split in same ratio.
mistakes: Splitting equally instead of by rate

practice.question: 20 men can do work in 50 days. Work done by 70 men in 5 days?
A and B together in 15 days; B alone in 20. A alone?
10 men do work in 12 days. 12 men?
A takes 50% more time than B. Together 18 days. B alone?
A+B in 3 days. Work 2 days together, B leaves, completed 2 more days. B alone?
practice.explanation: In 2 days A+B do 2/3. Remaining 1/3 done by A in 2 days → A alone = 6 days. A+B = 1/3 per day → B = 1/3 − 1/6 = 1/6 → B alone = 6 days.

practice.question: A can finish a job in 10 days. Fraction of work done per day =
practice.explanation: Rate = 1 job / 10 days = 1/10 of the job per day (work rates, not days, are additive).

practice.question: If 6 workers finish a job in 8 days, total work measured in worker-days =
practice.explanation: Work = workers * days = 6 * 8 = 48 worker-days - a conserved quantity used in every chain-rule work problem.

questions.question: A and B together complete work in 18 days. A and C together in 12 days. B and C together in 9 days. B alone?
A and B together complete work in 3 days. After 2 days B left. Completed 2 more days. B alone?
questions.explanation: A+B do 2/3 in 2 days. Remaining 1/3 done by A in 2 days → A = 6 days. A+B = 1/3/day → B = 1/3 − 1/6 = 1/6 → B alone = 6 days.

questions.question: A takes 50% more time than B. Together 18 days. B alone?
Working 5 hrs/day, A completes work in 8 days. B same work 6 hrs/day in 10 days. Working 8 hrs/day together?
questions.explanation: A: 5×8=40 hr-work. B: 6×10=60 hr-work. Combined rate per hour = 1/40 + 1/60 = (3+2)/120 = 5/120 = 1/24 work/hr. Together = 24 hrs work. At 8 hrs/day → 3 days.

questions.question: 10 men or 20 boys make 260 mats in 20 days. 8 men and 4 boys in 20 days?
questions.explanation: 10 men = 20 boys → 1 man = 2 boys. 8 men + 4 boys = 16+4 = 20 boys. 20 boys make 260 mats in 20 days → 260 mats.

questions.question: A does a job in 12 days, B in 18 days. Working together, time taken =
questions.explanation: Combined rate = 1/12 + 1/18 = 3/36 + 2/36 = 5/36 per day. Time = 36/5 = 7.2 days.

questions.question: A is twice as fast as B. If B alone finishes a job in 20 days, A and B together take:
questions.explanation: B's rate = 1/20, A's rate = 2/20 = 1/10. Together = 1/20 + 1/10 = 3/20 per day, so time = 20/3 = 6.67 days.

questions.question: 10 workers can build a wall in 12 days. After 4 days, 6 more workers join. Remaining work finishes in:
questions.explanation: Total work = 10 * 12 = 120 worker-days. Done in the first 4 days = 10 * 4 = 40, so 80 worker-days remain. Crew becomes 10 + 6 = 16 workers: 80 / 16 = 5 days.
